humanAuthorship.title: Human Authorship pledge
humanAuthorship.why: Why we ask: the AUIB Literary Journal, the Prizes and Scratch Night judge work as the member's own. This pledge is what keeps that fair to everyone who submits.
humanAuthorship.body: Creative work submitted to Society programmes (AUIB Literary Journal, the Prizes, Scratch Night, the Typewriter Tour) must be the member’s own. Work drafted, written, translated or generated by AI is not eligible. Spellcheck and basic grammar tools are fine. (Policy Manual, SAL-POL-01, P10.1)

member.title: Member Pledge (SAL-POL-01)
member.why: Why we ask: every member signs it. It's the promise that keeps the Society's rooms, events and channels kind and safe for everyone.
member.body: As a member of the Society of Arts and Letters, I will treat everyone with courtesy and every piece of work with care. I will critique the work and never the person. I will respect consent, before a camera and on the page. I will be honest with the Society’s money and its members’ trust. I will keep what is confidential, keep my word or say early that I cannot, and leave every room better than I found it.

agreement.title: Publication Agreement
agreement.body:
By signing, you agree to the Society's terms for publishing your work, from the Policy Manual (SAL-POL-01):

9.1 Creators own their work. By presenting or submitting it, they give the Society permission to show, perform, publish and archive it for the purpose agreed, and nothing more.

9.2 Everyone who works on a Society project is credited by name in its programme, masthead or end credits, unless they ask not to be.

9.5 Plagiarism in any Society programme leads to withdrawal of the work and may lead to action under P1.

10.1 Creative work submitted to Society programmes (AUIB Literary Journal, the Prizes, Scratch Night, the Typewriter Tour) must be the member’s own. Work drafted, written, translated or generated by AI is not eligible. Spellcheck and basic grammar tools are fine.

The purpose agreed is publication in AUIB Literary Journal, online and in print, and the Society's archive.

f04.title: Interview Score Sheet
f04.purpose: Each panel member scores alone, then the panel agrees. Fifteen minutes per interview.
f04.preamble: Ask every candidate the same questions: 1. Tell us about something you made or organised that you are proud of. 2. What would you do in your first month in this role? 3. Tell us about a time a team member let you down. What did you do? 4. This role needs [x] hours a week. What will you drop in a busy week? 5. How would you make someone who speaks only Arabic, or only English, feel welcome? 6. What questions do you have for us? Score 1 = not shown · 3 = solid · 5 = outstanding.

fields.score_skills: Relevant skills (25%): has done, or can quickly learn, what the role needs
fields.score_ideas: Ideas for the role (20%): concrete, fits the mission, not only big
fields.score_teamwork: Teamwork and care (20%): listens, credits others, handles pressure kindly
fields.score_values: Fit with our values (15%): open door, craft, both languages, care, honesty

about.title: About the Society
about.lede: To cultivate a culture of literature and creative expression across AUIB.
about.draftNote: Quoted from the draft Constitution (SAL-GOV-01), which the Founding General Assembly is asked to ratify on Charter Day.
about.preamble: We, students of the American University of Iraq – Baghdad, gathered as the Society of Arts and Letters, in a city that once kept the House of Wisdom and still keeps al-Mutanabbi Street, adopt this Constitution so that our Society is open to every student, governed in the open, careful with people and money, and built to outlast those who founded it.
about.mottoNote: From al-Mutanabbi's most quoted line: the horses, the night and the desert know me; so do the sword, the lance, the paper and the pen. We keep only the last two.

connecting.title: Connecting students
connecting.body: From every college, into one room and onto one page.

fostering.title: Fostering creativity
fostering.body: Deadlines, editors and stages that turn drafts into finished work.

celebrating.title: Celebrating culture
celebrating.body: Arabic and English side by side; Iraqi writing next to world writing.

building.title: Building a community
building.body: A society people stay in, and come back to.

open.title: Open and free
open.body: Any enrolled AUIB student can join. No fee, no audition, no portfolio. Members who take part in two activities a semester vote.

power.title: Members hold the power
power.body: The General Assembly of all members elects the officers, changes this Constitution and can remove anyone who abuses a role.

council.title: A Council runs the work
council.body: Four elected officers and six appointed directors meet every two weeks, adopt the budget and greenlight programs.

elections.title: Elections every April
elections.body: Secret ballot with AUIB sign-in, run by a committee of non-candidates. Ranked choice when more than two stand. Presidents serve two terms at most.

editors.title: Editors decide the art
editors.body: Program editors and directors make creative calls. The Council overrules a selection only on grounds of law, safety or University policy, and in writing.

money.title: Every dinar is logged
money.body: Spending limits, two people on every cash count, receipts for everything, and charity money passed on in full.

process.title: Fair process
process.body: Anyone facing discipline hears the concern and can answer it. Removal of an officer needs two-thirds of members voting.

last.title: Written to last
last.body: Minutes, reports and an archive are kept for the next generation. Core principles can only be changed at two meetings, a month apart.

about.nonPartisan: Our Society is non-partisan and non-sectarian. Your writing and art can explore anything human. The Society itself takes no side in party or sect.

join.title: Join the Society
join.lede: Membership is free and open to every AUIB student. There is no audition, no portfolio and no fee.

register.title: Register
register.body: Sign up in the Nexus with your AUIB email and sign the Member Pledge.

commonRoom.title: Join The Common Room
commonRoom.body: Our Telegram channel, where reminders and room changes go first. Follow @auibsal too.

twoThings.title: Come to two things
twoThings.body: Any two Society activities in a semester make you a Voting Member: you can vote in elections and stand for office. For the founding year, the first 100 members vote from the day they join.

member.name: Member
member.can: take part in everything, pitch ideas, apply for roles

voting.name: Voting Member
voting.if: took part in two activities this or last semester
voting.can: also vote and stand for election

fellow.name: Fellow
fellow.if: gave outstanding service, named by the Council
fellow.can: keep the title for life; your name in the Book of Fellows

honorary.name: Honorary Member
honorary.if: are faculty, staff, an alumnus or a guest artist honored by the Council
honorary.can: join us as a friend and guest (no vote)

alumni.name: Alumni Member
alumni.can: come back to Charter Night and mentor

join.firstMonth: Register · join The Common Room · type your six words · come to a Majlis with your buddy · tell us after your second event what you would like to do here.

programmes.title: Programs
programmes.lede: Four big programs and a rhythm of small ones. The Term Card lists this semester's dates.

give.title: Give
give.lede: Second Chapter, the charity book drive and fair, every fall. Edition 1: November 1–11, 2026.
give.waysNote: We take no payments online. Give in person at the drive and the fair, where every amount is counted and recorded.
give.noCampaign: No campaign is running at the moment.
give.perSet: One child's winter set costs about {amount} (to be confirmed).
give.transparencyLede: Every dinar is counted twice and reported.
give.policy: Charity money is held separately, never used for costs, and handed over in full at a witnessed handover with a receipt.
give.countedNote: The Warmth Meter shows only money that two people have counted and a second officer has signed off.

contact.title: Contact
contact.lede: Find us on Instagram and in The Common Room, or talk to us at any event.
contact.emailPending: The Society's email address will be listed here.
contact.concern: If something is wrong, tell any officer, our Faculty Advisor or the Office of Student Life, in person or with the concern form. Harassment, safety and anything involving a child go straight to Student Life.
contact.photoTitle: A photo or video of you
contact.photo: Ask and it comes down within 24 hours.

mediaKit.title: Media kit
mediaKit.lede: The Society's name, logos and colors, for partners and the press.
mediaKit.name: "AUIB Society of Arts and Letters" in full on first use in formal documents; then "the Society" or "SAL". Never "the club".
mediaKit.programmeLine: Endorsed programs carry the line "a Society of Arts and Letters programme".
mediaKit.about: The AUIB Society of Arts and Letters is a student society at the American University of Iraq – Baghdad. Its mission is to cultivate a culture of literature and creative expression across AUIB.
mediaKit.logosNote: Use the files exactly as supplied. Never stretch, recolor, rotate, re-break the wordmark lines, add effects or shadows, or put the crimson symbol on ink. Where the AUIB logo appears it leads, and the SAL lockup follows at equal or smaller height.
mediaKit.contactPress: For anything else, contact the Media Director through any of our channels.

privacy.title: Privacy and photo policy
privacy.lede: How the Society treats your data and your image, from the Policy Manual, and how this website and the Nexus handle your information.

p.5_1: Anyone clearly featured in Society video or photography, or in an interview, signs a release (Form F-17) before publication. Guests see their episode or feature before it is released.
p.5_2: At every event, a notice says that photography is taking place. Anyone may wear a camera-shy sticker or ask not to be photographed; photographers respect this without question.
p.5_3: Anyone may ask for a photo or video of themselves to be removed. The Society takes it down within 24 hours, no reasons needed.
p.5_4: Crowd photographs are fine; close-ups of individuals who have not agreed are not published.
p.5_5: Photographs of people praying, in distress or in private moments are not taken.
p.6_1: The Society collects only what it needs: name, AUIB email, college, year, phone (optional), and attendance. It never collects ID numbers or bank details.
p.6_2: Member data lives in the restricted Members folder, seen only by the officers, the Director of Membership and the Records Lead.
p.6_3: Member data is never shared outside the Society or used for anything other than Society business, including campaigning in Society elections.
p.6_4: Members may ask to see or delete their data at any time. Data of members who leave is deleted one year after they leave, except their name and roles in the archive.
p.6_5: Submissions, ballots and conduct records follow their own retention rules: AUIB Literary Journal's guidelines, B6.11 and B10.8.

platform.signIn: You sign in to the Nexus with your email address. The sign-in cookie is shared across auibsal.org and its subdomains, and is used only to keep you signed in.
platform.storage: Member records are stored with Supabase in the European Union (Frankfurt). Who can see each record is enforced in the database itself, by role.
platform.email: Email from the platform is sent by Resend from the European Union (Ireland). Links in it are not tracked.
platform.hosting: The website, the Nexus and the API are hosted on Vercel.
platform.analytics: This website uses no analytics or advertising cookies.
platform.delete: You can delete your account in the Nexus, under Profile and privacy.
platform.analyticsOn: This website uses Google Analytics 4 to count visits; it sets analytics cookies.

partners.title: Partners
partners.lede: The clubs, departments and organizations the AUIB Society of Arts and Letters works with. Every partnership listed here has a signed memorandum.
partners.empty: Our first partnerships are being agreed. They will appear here once signed.
partners.work: The Society partners with clubs, departments, charities and cultural organizations whose aims fit its mission and who treat people fairly. Sponsors are acknowledged and never have editorial influence. Write to the Director of Partnerships through the contact page.

verify.lede: Certificates from the AUIB Society of Arts and Letters carry a code at the foot. Type it to see whether the certificate stands.
verify.invalid: That doesn't look like a certificate code.
verify.notFound: No certificate has this code. Check it and try again.

verify.signedBy: Signed in the Nexus by the President and the Faculty Advisor.
